column3: Close to the Greek; “prostitutes” is rendered “harlots,” and “go before you into” as “enter … before you.”
Close to the Greek; “repent” is rendered “relent.”
Close to the Greek; “farmers” is rendered “vinedressers,” and “traveled abroad” as “went into a far country.”
Close to the Greek; “the season of the fruits” is rendered “vintage-time.”
Close to the Greek; “afterward” is rendered “last of all.”
NKJV has “seize his inheritance,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “have his inheritance.”
